# PURISTA LLM Full Context

## Primary reading order
1. https://github.com/puristajs/purista/blob/master/AGENTS.md
2. https://github.com/puristajs/purista/blob/master/skills/purista/SKILL.md
3. https://github.com/puristajs/purista/blob/master/web/src/content/handbook/index.md
4. https://github.com/puristajs/purista/blob/master/web/src/content/handbook/3_eco_system/index.md

## Service and distributed-system rules

- Begin with `ServiceBuilder`; obtain commands, subscriptions, streams, queues,
  workers, schedules, and attached agents through its builder methods.
- Use Zod schemas and versioned service directories. Keep handlers thin and
  resource-driven.
- Commands are request/response business actions. Events are immutable facts.
  Subscriptions react to facts. Queues provide asynchronous, retryable work.
  Streams provide progressive output. Do not interchange these semantics just
  because their TypeScript shapes are similar.
- Workers and schedule consumers must be idempotent. PURISTA does not promise
  exactly-once delivery or exactly-once external side effects.
- A scheduler host is separate deployment infrastructure that emits regular
  events; it never runs service business handlers. Use an external distributed
  scheduler provider when replicas can overlap.
- Run `purista inspect` and `purista validate --strict` before modifying an
  existing project. Their output is a static architecture projection and must
  not be represented as runtime/provider health.
- Keep tests adjacent to behavior. Update public TSDoc, handbook docs, skills,
  and generated knowledge whenever public behavior changes.
